technicalNotes.implementationNotes:
CRITICAL — argument parsing pitfall: use Number() not parseInt() to parse --adults. parseInt('1.5', 10) silently truncates to 1 (a valid integer), making the non-integer validation impossible — Number.isInteger(1) is true so exit code 2 is never triggered. Number('1.5') returns 1.5, which correctly fails Number.isInteger() and triggers exit 2. The adults validation must reject: non-integer values (e.g. 1.5), zero, negative numbers, and non-numeric strings. All must exit with code 2.

CRITICAL — separator row format: the table renders one hyphen-segment per column, padded to that column's width, separated by the same whitespace used between column values. The separator is NOT a single run of unbroken hyphens. A regex checking the separator must allow spaces: /^[-\s]+$/ not /^-[-]+$/.

CRITICAL — main() must be exported and guarded. Export the function: `export async function main()`. Guard execution: `if (require.main === module) { main(); }` or use the VITEST env var pattern. Unexported main cannot be tested via require('./cli').main.

notes:
Openspec provided empty criteria, so I built from the original story ACs with the following changes:

MODIFIED:
- AC 3 (required flags): Added 'whitespace-only' as equivalent to absent — `--from '   '` should not bypass validation.
- AC 5 (--adults): Removed the implementation detail 'via Number()' per the what-not-how rule; retained the observable behavior that 1.5 is rejected as non-integer.

ADDED:
- Separator row format criterion: The technical notes flag this as a critical pitfall — a single unbroken hyphen line is wrong; per-column hyphen segments with inter-column spacing is the correct observable output. Added as a separate AC for testability.
- Missing/empty field values in flight data: Ensures table alignment doesn't break when API returns incomplete records.
- RAPIDAPI_KEY not leaked to stdout: Security — credential must never appear in any stdout output path.
- main() exported: Testability requirement — without an exported main, the module cannot be tested via programmatic invocation.

FLAGGED:
- Behavior for unrecognized/unknown flags (e.g., `--foo bar`) is unspecified in the story. Should they be silently ignored or cause an error? Left for human decision.

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is absent on GET /search, the request succeeds (HTTP 200) with a default value of 1 passed to SkyscannerClient — `adults` is optional, not required

GET /cheapest with valid required query params (from, to, date) returns HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult whose `price` field is less than or equal to the `price` field of every FlightResult returned by SkyscannerClient for the same route/date (validated against a mocked client response); if `adults` is supplied it is forwarded, if absent it defaults to 1

The `searchedAt` field in the GET /search response is an ISO-8601 datetime string reflecting the time of the request (not a hardcoded value); successive requests separated by at least 1 ms return distinct values

before.description: Create src/server.ts — an Express HTTP server that exposes: (1) GET /health → { status: 'ok', uptime: number }, (2) GET /search?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01&adults=1 → { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string }, (3) GET /cheapest?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01 → the single cheapest FlightResult or 404 JSON { error: string } if none found, (4) GET / → serves src/public/index.html by reading the file at runtime (e.g. fs.readFileSync) — the handler must NOT hardcode a separate inline HTML string that merely happens to match; content and implementation must not be able to diverge. Server reads PORT from env (default 3000); reads RAPIDAPI_KEY from env and passes to SkyscannerClient. If RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at startup all API routes (/search, /cheapest) return 503 { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; /health and / are never gated. The listen() call must be guarded so importing `app` in tests does not bind a port. Add 'start' script in package.json pointing to 'node dist/server.js'. Install supertest and @types/supertest. Create src/server.test.ts using vitest + supertest with at least 8 tests covering the scenarios in acceptance criteria. Depends on SKY-002 (SkyscannerClient and FlightResult type must exist before this story is started). The build script must copy src/public/ (or equivalent static assets) into dist/public/ as part of `npm run build`, since tsc alone does not copy non-.ts files — the file path used by the /  route handler must resolve correctly both under `tsx src/server.ts` (dev) and `node dist/server.js` (built).

splitStories.title: Core Express API routes: /health, /search, /cheapest with RAPIDAPI_KEY gating
splitStories.description: Implement src/server.ts with Express app exporting `app` separately from a port-guarded listen(). Wire /health, /search, /cheapest routes with param validation, SkyscannerClient delegation, RAPIDAPI_KEY gating middleware, and error handling. Import FlightResult from SKY-002.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) separately from the `listen()` call so supertest can import it without binding a port

The `listen()` call is guarded by `if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)` (ESM) or `if (require.main === module)` (CJS) matching the tsup output format so `vitest run` never binds a port
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> } regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY is set or absent

GET /search with valid params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 } where count === flights.length and searchedAt is distinct per request; adults defaults to 1 if absent; missing required param (from/to/date) → 400 { error }; non-numeric adults → 400 { error }

GET /cheapest with valid params returns HTTP 200 with the single cheapest FlightResult (price ≤ all others); adults defaults to 1 if absent; empty results → 404 { error }; missing required param → 400 { error }

When RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at initialisation, a single middleware short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected
When SkyscannerClient throws during /search or /cheapest, the server returns HTTP 500 { error: string } without crashing or emitting an unhandled promise rejection
FlightResult type is imported from the SKY-002 export (e.g. src/skyscanner/client.ts), not redeclared inline

splitStories.title: Static dashboard HTML and build/start configuration
splitStories.description: Create src/public/index.html as a styled single-page dashboard with search form and client-side JS. Wire GET / to serve it via fs.readFileSync at runtime. Configure package.json build script to copy static assets to dist/public/ and add start script. Add supertest devDependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: src/public/index.html exists as a styled dashboard with: (1) full-width solid-color header bar (e.g. #1a73e8) with bold white title 'Skyscanner Dashboard' and subtitle; (2) centered white card (max-width ~700px, rounded corners) with 2-column grid search form: From/To IATA inputs row 1, Date/Adults inputs row 2, each with label; (3) full-width colored 'Search Flights' button; (4) status area with red error banner, gray empty message, success count; (5) client-side JS submitting GET /search via fetch, disabling button during request, rendering results table in-page

GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html and body equal to contents of src/public/index.html read at runtime via fs.readFileSync — hardcoded inline HTML is NOT acceptable; this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY
package.json contains a 'start' script with value 'node dist/server.js'
package.json 'build' script produces dist/server.js such that `npm run build && npm run start` starts the server and GET /health returns HTTP 200
Build script copies src/public/ into dist/public/ — after `npm run build`, dist/public/index.html exists and GET / serves the real dashboard file (not 404 or hardcoded fallback)
supertest and @types/supertest are listed in package.json devDependencies
`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no type errors
The file path used by the GET / handler resolves correctly under both `tsx src/server.ts` (dev) and `node dist/server.js` (built)

splitStories.title: Server test suite with supertest and mocked SkyscannerClient
splitStories.description: Create src/server.test.ts with ≥8 vitest tests using supertest against the exported app. Mock SkyscannerClient so no real HTTP calls are made. Cover all API route scenarios from SKY-004-A and the dashboard route from SKY-004-B.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server.test.ts contains ≥8 distinct vitest test cases covering: /health (200, ungated by RAPIDAPI_KEY), /search valid params (200 with correct structure), /search missing required param (400), /search adults default/invalid, /cheapest valid (200 cheapest flight), /cheapest empty results (404), /cheapest missing params (400), RAPIDAPI_KEY absent (503 on /search and /cheapest), SkyscannerClient error (500), GET / (200 HTML from file)
All SkyscannerClient calls are mocked via vi.mock or equivalent — no real HTTP calls during vitest run
Tests use supertest against the exported `app` without binding a port
`vitest run` exits 0 with all tests passing
Delegated to split children: SKY-004-A, SKY-004-B, SKY-004-C

acceptanceCriteria: The server module exports a named `app` (Express Application) that can be imported without starting the HTTP listener; the listener only starts when the module is run as the main entry point
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> } regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY is set or absent

GET /search with valid params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 } where count === flights.length; adults defaults to 1 if omitted; missing required param (from, to, or date) returns 400 with { error }; non-numeric adults returns 400 with { error }

GET /cheapest with valid params returns HTTP 200 with the single cheapest FlightResult (price ≤ all others); adults defaults to 1 if omitted; empty results return 404 with { error }; missing required param returns 400 with { error }
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent, GET /search and GET /cheapest return HTTP 503 with body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / remain unaffected (return 200)
When SkyscannerClient throws during /search or /cheapest, the server returns HTTP 500 with body { error: string } without crashing or emitting an unhandled promise rejection

GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html and body equal to the contents of the dashboard HTML file read from disk at runtime (not hardcoded inline); this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY

The dashboard HTML contains a styled search form with labeled From, To, Date, and Adults inputs, a Search Flights button, and client-side JavaScript that submits GET /search via fetch and renders results in-page
After `npm run build`, dist/server.js exists and `npm run start` starts the server where GET /health returns HTTP 200; dist/public/index.html exists and GET / serves the dashboard file

The test suite contains ≥8 distinct test cases covering all API route scenarios and the dashboard route; no real HTTP calls to Skyscanner are made during test execution; `npm test` exits 0 with all tests passing
Error responses (400, 404, 500, 503) do not expose stack traces or internal implementation details in the response body
GET /search and /cheapest reject adults values of 0 or negative numbers with 400 { error }
If the dashboard HTML file is absent at runtime, GET / returns HTTP 500 without crashing the server process
The dashboard HTML includes a lang attribute on the <html> element, label elements associated with all form inputs via matching for/id attributes, and a submit button with descriptive text

after.title: Build Express REST API with /health, /search, /cheapest, and static dashboard endpoints

notes: Refined all 9 of openspec's top-level ACs for specificity: added exact HTTP status codes, Content-Type headers, response body shapes, and error message text where missing. Expanded vague criteria (e.g. 'validates params' → explicit param names and 400 behavior; 'returns 200 JSON { status, uptime }' → specifies status value 'ok' and uptime as positive number). Removed implementation instructions from child ACs that violated WHAT-NOT-HOW: replaced 'guarded by if (import.meta.url === …)' with observable outcome 'listener only starts when module is run as main entry point'; replaced 'mocked via vi.mock' with 'no real HTTP calls to Skyscanner during test execution'; replaced 'use supertest against exported app' with the testable outcome of ≥8 tests passing without port binding. Added 4 new criteria: (11) no stack trace leakage in error responses — security; (12) adults=0/negative rejection — edge case; (13) missing dashboard file graceful error — error handling; (14) dashboard accessibility basics (lang, labels, button text) — accessibility.
